sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanthan.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Millions of us try to lose weight every year.
sentences.zh: 每年有数百万人尝试减肥。

sentences.en: We go on diets, read books, buy pills off the internet.
sentences.zh: 我们节食、读书、从网上买减肥药。

sentences.en: Collectively, we spend billions of dollars trying to slim down.
sentences.zh: 我们总共花费了数十亿美元试图瘦下来。

sentences.en: And the truth is, we might as well flush a lot of that money down the toilet.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我们还不如把这些钱直接冲进马桶里。

sentences.en: All those workouts, challenges, and temptations come down.
sentences.zh: 所有那些锻炼、挑战和诱惑都归结于此。

sentences.en: With thousands of diets out there, they've all chosen...
sentences.zh: 市面上有成千上万种节食法，但它们都选择了……

sentences.en: Jack was trying to teach me sugar equals pain.
sentences.zh: 杰克试图教导我，糖分等于痛苦。

sentences.en: Yes, I was miserable.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时痛苦不堪。

sentences.en: As they say in the infomercials, there must be a better way.
sentences.zh: 正如电视购物广告里所说，一定有更好的方法。

sentences.en: This week, we're going to talk about psychological tricks we can play on ourselves
sentences.zh: 本周，我们将讨论我们可以对自己使用的心理小技巧，

sentences.en: to help us eat better and to follow through on our best intentions.
sentences.zh: 以帮助我们吃得更好，并坚持我们最好的初衷。

sentences.en: My name is Adam Brumberg.
sentences.zh: 我叫亚当·布伦伯格。

sentences.en: I am the Deputy Director of the Cornell Food and Brand Lab at Cornell University.
sentences.zh: 我是康奈尔大学康奈尔食品与品牌实验室的副主任。

sentences.en: Adam Brumberg and his colleagues research food psychology,
sentences.zh: 亚当·布伦伯格和他的同事们研究食品心理学，

sentences.en: and they find that many of our food choices aren't really conscious choices.
sentences.zh: 他们发现我们许多的饮食选择并非真正的有意识选择。

sentences.en: The majority of your food decisions are based on habit or convenience.
sentences.zh: 你大部分的饮食决定是基于习惯或便利。

sentences.en: You know, habit being, I did it yesterday, worked out fine, I'm going to do it again.
sentences.zh: 你知道，习惯就是：我昨天这么做了，效果不错，所以我打算再做一次。

sentences.en: And convenience, well, I'm sitting at my desk and there is a package of ringdings on the desk
sentences.zh: 而便利就是：我坐在办公桌前，桌上有一包零食，

sentences.en: and so I'm just going to eat that instead of going and finding something that's healthier.
sentences.zh: 所以我干脆就吃那个，而不是去寻找更健康的东西。

sentences.en: Once you understand these bad, unconscious patterns, you could stay on guard, use willpower to fight them.
sentences.zh: 一旦你理解了这些糟糕的无意识模式，你就可以保持警惕，用意志力去对抗它们。

sentences.en: But there's also a smarter way.
sentences.zh: 但也有更聪明的方法。

sentences.en: You could turn the tables and get these unconscious habits to work for you.
sentences.zh: 你可以扭转局面，让这些无意识的习惯为你所用。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, we like to say that the best diet is the one you don't know you're on.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我们喜欢说最好的节食就是你根本没意识到自己在节食。

sentences.en: Our research shows that you make about 200 food-related decisions a day, which is a lot.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究表明，你每天大约会做出200个与食物相关的决定，这非常多。

sentences.en: By food decisions, Adam doesn't just mean whether you eat a salad or a sandwich.
sentences.zh: 亚当所说的“饮食决定”不仅仅是指你吃沙拉还是三明治。

sentences.en: It's also, how much salt do you put on your food?
sentences.zh: 还包括：你在食物里放多少盐？

sentences.en: Do you have a slice of cake when your co-worker celebrates a birthday?
sentences.zh: 当同事庆祝生日时，你会吃一块蛋糕吗？

sentences.en: Do you reward yourself for going to the gym with a cookie?
sentences.zh: 你会因为去健身房锻炼而奖励自己一块饼干吗？

sentences.en: Here's one example of how you can turn the tables on your unconscious habits.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个关于如何扭转无意识习惯的例子。

sentences.en: Adam and his colleagues find that volunteers in lab experiments make worse choices when they're stressed.
sentences.zh: 亚当和他的同事发现，实验室实验中的志愿者在压力大时会做出更糟糕的选择。

sentences.en: The stressed out folks were more likely to buy a dessert or to select a fried item as opposed to
sentences.zh: 压力大的人更有可能购买甜点或选择油炸食品，而不是……

sentences.en: that people asked to think of things they were grateful for.
sentences.zh: 那些被要求去想让他们感恩之事的受试者。

sentences.en: They were more likely to get salad or grilled chicken or whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能选择沙拉、烤鸡或类似的东西。

sentences.en: Once you understand how stress shapes mindless eating,
sentences.zh: 一旦你理解了压力是如何塑造无意识饮食的，

sentences.en: you can set up a system, when you're not stressed, that allows you to take advantage of this tendency.
sentences.zh: 你就可以在没有压力的时候建立一套系统，让你利用这种倾向。

sentences.en: If you pack a lunch the night before, you're definitely going to put together something that's a lot more helpful
sentences.zh: 如果你在前一天晚上打包好午餐，你肯定会准备一些更有益的东西，

sentences.en: than if you are doing it as you're running out of the house in the morning.
sentences.zh: 这比你早上匆忙出门时现做要好得多。

sentences.en: Now, Adam Brumberg says, when you're stressed out at work and mindlessly reaching for something to eat,
sentences.zh: 现在，亚当·布伦伯格说，当你在工作中感到压力大，无意识地伸手去拿东西吃时，

sentences.en: your hand's going to come up with a carrot rather than a ringling.
sentences.zh: 你的手会拿到胡萝卜而不是零食。

sentences.en: You have to work really hard to eat too many baby carrots.
sentences.zh: 你得非常努力才能吃下过多的胡萝卜条。

sentences.en: We decided to devote this whole episode to ideas like this.
sentences.zh: 我们决定把这一整集都献给这类想法。

sentences.en: Coming up in a moment, senior Stopwatch Science correspondent Dan Pink and I
sentences.zh: 稍后，资深“秒表科学”记者丹·平克和我

sentences.en: are going to trade psychological tricks that might help your actual waistline look like the one you want.
sentences.zh: 将交流一些心理小技巧，帮助你的腰围看起来如你所愿。

sentences.en: Behavioral science has given us lots of tricks for eating less.
sentences.zh: 行为科学为我们提供了许多少吃的技巧。

sentences.en: Smaller plates, smaller portions, but a new study this year in the Journal of the Association of Consumer Research
sentences.zh: 用更小的盘子，更小的份量，但今年《消费者研究协会杂志》上的一项新研究

sentences.en: offers another option, larger tables.
sentences.zh: 提供了另一种选择：更大的桌子。

sentences.en: So pull up a chair at a big table and stay with us.
sentences.zh: 所以，拉把椅子坐在大桌子旁，继续收听我们的节目。

sentences.en: Support for Hidden Brain and the following message comes from Wells Fargo.
sentences.zh: 《隐藏的大脑》及以下信息由富国银行提供支持。

sentences.en: Wells Fargo understands that you work hard to get the most out of life.
sentences.zh: 富国银行了解你为充分享受生活而努力工作。

sentences.en: From starting a business to saving for retirement, there are a lot of things you want to accomplish.
sentences.zh: 从创业到为退休储蓄，有很多事情你想完成。

sentences.en: Working together, Wells Fargo will take the time to understand what you're trying to achieve
sentences.zh: 通过合作，富国银行将花时间了解你想要实现的目标，

sentences.en: to help you reach your financial goals.
sentences.zh: 以帮助你达成财务目标。

sentences.en: That way you can care for the people and things that matter moSt.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以照顾好最重要的人和事。

sentences.en: Learn more at wellsfargo.com slash together.
sentences.zh: 了解更多信息，请访问 wellsfargo.com/together。

sentences.en: Wells Fargo.
sentences.zh: 富国银行。

sentences.en: Together we'll go far.
sentences.zh: 携手共进，行稳致远。

sentences.en: Support also comes from Atlassian.
sentences.zh: 节目也得到了Atlassian的支持。

sentences.en: Today nearly anything is possible.
sentences.zh: 今天，几乎一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: And if we can dream it, teams can build it.
sentences.zh: 只要我们敢想，团队就能做到。

sentences.en: Jira, Confluence, HipChat, and Bitbucket give your team everything you need to organize, discuss, and complete shared work.
sentences.zh: Jira、Confluence、HipChat和Bitbucket为你的团队提供了组织、讨论和完成共享工作所需的一切。

sentences.en: Atlassian works to help teams large and small ascend to new heights to create what's next.
sentences.zh: Atlassian致力于帮助大大小小的团队攀登新高峰，创造未来。

sentences.en: Visit Atlassian.com.
sentences.zh: 请访问 Atlassian.com。

sentences.en: Atlassian.
sentences.zh: 阿特拉斯扬公司。

sentences.en: Team up.
sentences.zh: 团队协作。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Summer is around the corner, which means beaches and swimsuits are around the corner too.
sentences.zh: 夏天即将来临，这意味着海滩和泳装也快到了。

sentences.en: Today, with a view to getting myself into beach-ready shape, I've asked Daniel Pink to come in to trade psychological tricks on how to eat better.
sentences.zh: 今天，为了让我自己达到海滩身材，我邀请了丹尼尔·平克来交流关于如何吃得更好的心理小技巧。

sentences.en: We're also going to look at some surprising factors that make us eat worse.
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨一些导致我们吃得更糟的惊人因素。

sentences.en: Dan, of course, is our senior stopwatch science correspondent, or actually I should say our svelte senior stopwatch science correspondent.
sentences.zh: 丹当然是我们资深的“秒表科学”记者，或者我应该说，是我们苗条的资深“秒表科学”记者。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dan.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，丹。

sentences.en: Thank you, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Now, I would say my body is beach-ready on the radio.
sentences.zh: 现在，我会说我的身材在广播里看起来很适合去海滩。

sentences.en: What about yours, Dan?
sentences.zh: 你呢，丹？

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I don't really think in those terMs.
sentences.zh: 我真的不会那样想。

sentences.en: I tend to go out in public fully, if not heavily clothed.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于在公共场合穿得严严实实，甚至穿得很厚。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Now, as you know, on Stopwatch Science, Dan and I give one another 60 seconds to summarize interesting social science research.
sentences.zh: 现在，如你所知，在“秒表科学”节目中，丹和我给对方60秒的时间来总结有趣的社会科学研究。

sentences.en: As we approach the 60-second mark, our producers will bring up the music just like they do at the Oscars.
sentences.zh: 当我们接近60秒大关时，我们的制作人会像奥斯卡颁奖典礼那样响起音乐。

sentences.en: Dan and I will each present three different pieces of social science research.
sentences.zh: 丹和我将各自介绍三项不同的社会科学研究。

sentences.en: We'll also spend a little more time between the segments unpacking the science and its implications.
sentences.zh: 我们还会在环节之间花更多时间来剖析科学及其含义。

sentences.en: Our topic today is dieting and the many ways in which hidden and unconscious factors shape our diets.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的主题是节食，以及隐藏和无意识因素塑造我们饮食的多种方式。

sentences.en: Dan, if you're ready, your first 60 seconds starts now.
sentences.zh: 丹，如果你准备好了，你的第一个60秒现在开始。

sentences.en: Behavioral science has given us lots of tricks for eating less.
sentences.zh: 行为科学为我们提供了许多少吃的技巧。

sentences.en: Smaller plates, smaller portions.
sentences.zh: 用更小的盘子，更小的份量。

sentences.en: But a new study this year in the Journal of the Association of Consumer Research offers another option, larger tables.
sentences.zh: 但今年《消费者研究协会杂志》上的一项新研究提供了另一种选择：更大的桌子。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: For these experiments, researchers got a bunch of pizzas and a bunch more college students.
sentences.zh: 在这些实验中，研究人员准备了一堆披萨和更多的大学生。

sentences.en: They found that students consumed the least amount of pizza when they were served small slices on a large table.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，当学生们在大桌子上吃到小块披萨时，他们的披萨摄入量最少。

sentences.en: Sounds weird, but there's a good explanation.
sentences.zh: 听起来很奇怪，但有一个很好的解释。

sentences.en: When students saw the small slices on a tiny table, they quickly noticed just how measly those slices were.
sentences.zh: 当学生们看到小桌子上的小块披萨时，他们很快就注意到这些披萨块是多么寒酸。

sentences.en: So, of course, they grabbed more.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，他们拿得更多。

sentences.en: But when those same small slices were on a big table, their attention shifted away from the smallness of the pizza slices and toward the largeness of the table.
sentences.zh: 但当同样的小块披萨放在大桌子上时，他们的注意力从披萨块的小转移到了桌子的大上。

sentences.en: On a large table, the small slices seemed not so measly after all.
sentences.zh: 在大桌子上，小块披萨看起来似乎没那么寒酸了。

sentences.en: So students didn't feel the need to pile as many on their plate and ended up consuming less pizza overall.
sentences.zh: 所以学生们觉得没必要在盘子里堆那么多，最终总共吃的披萨更少了。

sentences.en: The lesson here?
sentences.zh: 这里的教训是什么？

sentences.en: Large tables may prevent large people.
sentences.zh: 大桌子或许能防止大块头。

sentences.en: All right, Dan, I have a question.
sentences.zh: 好吧，丹，我有个问题。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: So are the researchers saying that the fact that we see these pizza slices differently on small tables versus large tables, are they saying this is because of an optical illusion?
sentences.zh: 所以研究人员是说，我们在小桌子和大桌子上对披萨块的看法不同，是因为视错觉吗？

sentences.en: A little bit of an optical illusion.
sentences.zh: 有一点视错觉的成分。

sentences.en: The way our vision works is that we don't see things in absolute terMs.
sentences.zh: 我们视觉的工作方式是，我们不是以绝对术语来看待事物的。

sentences.en: We see them in relative terMs.
sentences.zh: 我们是以相对术语来看待它们的。

sentences.en: So when you have small slices on a tiny table, you can actually see how small those slices are.
sentences.zh: 所以当你把小块披萨放在小桌子上时，你确实能看出那些披萨块有多小。

sentences.en: But on a big table, everything looks about the same size because there's greater contraSt.
sentences.zh: 但在大桌子上，一切看起来大小差不多，因为对比度更高。

sentences.en: Therefore, people on the big table will eat the small slices.
sentences.zh: 因此，在大桌子旁的人会吃那些小块披萨。

sentences.en: They'll eat fewer of them and consume less pizza in total.
sentences.zh: 他们会吃得更少，总共摄入的披萨也更少。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: So Shankar, you and I are sitting here at a large table ourselves, so why don't you give us a small idea?
sentences.zh: 所以尚卡尔，你和我正坐在一张大桌子旁，你为什么不给我们出一个小点子呢？

sentences.en: I'm going to give you a small portion of an idea, Dan.
sentences.zh: 我会给你一小份点子，丹。

sentences.en: A small slice.
sentences.zh: 一小块。

sentences.en: It's going to fit in 60 seconds.
sentences.zh: 它会在60秒内讲完。

sentences.en: It turns out it isn't just the size of your dining table that influences how much you eat.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，影响你吃多少的不仅仅是餐桌的大小。

sentences.en: Your dining companions might make a difference, too.
sentences.zh: 你的用餐同伴也可能产生影响。

sentences.en: I did a story about this for NPR some time ago.
sentences.zh: 我前段时间为NPR做过一篇关于这个的报道。

sentences.en: Molly Allen O'Donnell told me that when she was a graduate student at Indiana University of Pennsylvania,
sentences.zh: 莫莉·艾伦·奥唐奈告诉我，当她在宾夕法尼亚州印第安纳大学读研究生时，

sentences.en: she sat down in a college cafeteria and looked at how much food people bought for lunch and dinner.
sentences.zh: 她坐在大学食堂里，观察人们午餐和晚餐买了多少食物。

sentences.en: She noticed that when women sat with other women, they ordered on average 833 calories of food.
sentences.zh: 她注意到，当女性与其他女性坐在一起时，她们平均点了833卡路里的食物。

sentences.en: When they sat with men, they ordered only 721 calories.
sentences.zh: 当她们与男性坐在一起时，她们只点了721卡路里。

sentences.en: So women ate more when they ate with women, and they ate less when they ate with men.
sentences.zh: 所以女性和女性一起吃饭时吃得更多，和男性一起吃饭时吃得更少。

sentences.en: Now, what about men?
sentences.zh: 那么男性呢？

sentences.en: I hear you asking the question, Dan.
sentences.zh: 我听见你在问这个问题了，丹。

sentences.en: What about men?
sentences.zh: 男性呢？

sentences.en: When men sat with other men, they ordered 952 calories.
sentences.zh: 当男性与其他男性坐在一起时，他们点了952卡路里。

sentences.en: But when they sat with women, they ordered 1,162 calories.
sentences.zh: 但当他们与女性坐在一起时，他们点了1162卡路里。

sentences.en: So another way to put this is both men and women ate more when they ate with women,
sentences.zh: 所以换句话说，男性和女性在与女性一起进餐时都吃得更多，

sentences.en: and both men and women ate less when they ate with men.
sentences.zh: 而在与男性一起进餐时都吃得更少。

sentences.en: Now, I'm sure we're going to talk about why this might be the case, Dan.
sentences.zh: 现在，我相信我们会讨论为什么会这样，丹。

sentences.en: But I want to take a moment to shout out to every overweight, married, heterosexual man who is listening.
sentences.zh: 但我想要花点时间向每一位正在收听节目的超重、已婚、异性恋男性致意。

sentences.en: The next time your wife tells you to lose a few pounds, you might want to say, honey, it's your fault.
sentences.zh: 下次你妻子让你减掉几磅时，你或许可以对她说：亲爱的，这都怪你。

sentences.en: Oh, nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，真不错。

sentences.en: You know, I think it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: The takeaway for me is that if you want to lose weight, eat with men.
sentences.zh: 我的结论是，如果你想减肥，就和男人一起吃饭。

sentences.en: I think that is one.
sentences.zh: 我想这是一个办法。

sentences.en: But why is it?
sentences.zh: 但这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why do men eat so much around women?
sentences.zh: 为什么男人在女人身边吃那么多？

sentences.en: I don't think the study conclusively answers that question, Dan.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这项研究能确凿地回答这个问题，丹。

sentences.en: There was a related study that I saw by Kevin Niffin at Cornell University.
sentences.zh: 我看到过康奈尔大学凯文·尼芬做过一项相关研究。

sentences.en: He and his colleagues found that men eat 93% more pizza and 86% more salad when eating with a woman compared to eating with a man.
sentences.zh: 他和他的同事发现，男性在与女性共餐时，披萨的摄入量比与男性共餐时多93%，沙拉多86%。

sentences.en: So it isn't just eating more unhealthy food.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是吃更多不健康的食物。

sentences.en: It's just eating more food in general.
sentences.zh: 而是总体上吃得更多。

sentences.en: Now, other studies have shown that heterosexual men in general tend to pursue more risky behaviors in the presence of women.
sentences.zh: 现在，其他研究表明，异性恋男性在女性面前通常倾向于进行更多冒险行为。

sentences.en: Studies show that mixed sex groups, for example, make more risky financial decisions.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，例如，混合性别群体会做出更多冒险的财务决策。

sentences.en: So it's possible that men are acting out some kind of evolutionary script by eating more food and demonstrating they're capable of riskier behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以，男性可能是在通过多吃食物并展示自己有能力进行更冒险的行为，来演绎某种进化剧本。

sentences.en: So they lose their inhibitions.
sentences.zh: 所以他们放下了戒备。

sentences.en: They show that I'm a big risk taker who can go out there and slay that saber-toothed tiger.
sentences.zh: 他们展示出：我是一个敢于冒险的人，可以出去猎杀那只剑齿虎。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So from my experience, back many, many years ago,
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，很多很多年前，

sentences.en: I would just be so psyched that a woman would be willing to eat with me that I'd probably lose my inhibitions and start gorging on pizza.
sentences.zh: 只要有女性愿意和我一起吃饭，我就会兴奋得不得了，以至于可能会放下戒备，开始大吃披萨。

sentences.en: You know, it may be that men who are able to eat a lot of food may have signaled some kind of evolutionary fitness in our ancient paSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这可能是因为在远古时代，能吃大量食物的男性可能预示着某种进化优势。

sentences.en: Now, of course, when food is so plentiful today, it might signal something else altogether.
sentences.zh: 当然，在食物如此充足的今天，这可能预示着完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: A lack of fitness.
sentences.zh: 预示着缺乏健康。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Let's see if you can signal to me that you can stick to your time, Dan.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看你能不能向我证明你能控制好时间，丹。

sentences.en: Your next 60 seconds starts right now.
sentences.zh: 你接下来的60秒现在开始。

sentences.en: You are what you eat.
sentences.zh: 人如其食。

sentences.en: We've all heard that.
sentences.zh: 我们都听过这句话。

sentences.en: But this next study shows you are also when you eat.
sentences.zh: 但接下来的这项研究表明，你什么时候吃也很重要。

sentences.en: Researchers at Tel Aviv University's medical school randomly assigned 93 overweight women into two groups.
sentences.zh: 特拉维夫大学医学院的研究人员随机将93名超重女性分成了两组。

sentences.en: Both groups ate the same food, 1,400 calories a day, not very much, for 12 weeks.
sentences.zh: 两组人每天摄入相同的食物，热量为1400卡路里，并不多，持续了12周。

sentences.en: But one group consumed half the calories at breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 但其中一组在早餐时摄入了一半的热量。

sentences.en: The other group consumed half the calories at dinner.
sentences.zh: 另一组在晚餐时摄入了一半的热量。

sentences.en: When the study was over, the big dinner group had lost an average of about seven pounds.
sentences.zh: 研究结束时，晚餐多吃的那一组平均减重约7磅。

sentences.en: Not bad.
sentences.zh: 还不错。

sentences.en: But the big breakfast group, those who ate the same food just earlier in the day, lost more than double that.
sentences.zh: 但早餐多吃的那一组，也就是在一天中较早时间吃同样食物的人，减掉的体重是前者的两倍多。

sentences.en: An average of more than 17 pounds.
sentences.zh: 平均减重超过17磅。

sentences.en: They also reduced their waistline more than the dinner group and even had greater drops in glucose, insulin, and triglycerides,
sentences.zh: 他们的腰围缩减程度也超过了晚餐组，甚至在血糖、胰岛素和甘油三酯水平上的下降幅度也更大，

sentences.en: high levels of which can lead to metabolic probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而这些指标水平过高会导致代谢问题。

sentences.en: Again, same food, same calories, just a different schedule.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，同样的食物，同样的热量，只是时间安排不同。

sentences.en: The bottom line, in eating as in life, timing is everything.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，饮食和生活一样，时机就是一切。

sentences.en: So what I find interesting about the study, Dan, is that it contradicts a view that I think many people hold,
sentences.zh: 丹，我觉得这项研究有趣的地方在于，它反驳了我认为许多人持有的一个观点，

sentences.en: which is that dieting is all just about calories in, calories out.
sentences.zh: 那就是节食完全取决于热量摄入和消耗。

sentences.en: Because what the study is suggesting is that it's not just about calories in, calories out.
sentences.zh: 因为这项研究表明，这不仅仅是热量摄入和消耗的问题。

sentences.en: It's when you eat those calories that can make a huge difference.
sentences.zh: 你摄入这些热量的时间可能会产生巨大的差异。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Our bodies are very, very complex systeMs.
sentences.zh: 我们的身体是非常、非常复杂的系统。

sentences.en: They don't work like simple machines.
sentences.zh: 它们不像简单的机器那样运作。

sentences.en: They're much more complex than that.
sentences.zh: 它们要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And a lot of endocrinologists, a lot of physicians are trying to figure out exactly what that right mix is.
sentences.zh: 许多内分泌学家和医生都在试图弄清楚到底什么是正确的组合。

sentences.en: But it turns out that questions of when can be just as important as questions of what.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，关于“何时”的问题可能和关于“吃什么”的问题一样重要。

sentences.en: Now, here's a what question for you.
sentences.zh: 现在，我有一个关于“吃什么”的问题要问你。

sentences.en: What do you got on your plate for your next study?
sentences.zh: 你接下来的研究打算探讨什么？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This next study will be of interest to anyone who hangs around with small kids.
sentences.zh: 接下来的这项研究会让任何与小孩相处的人感兴趣。

sentences.en: What's one way you get youngsters to eat healthy food?
sentences.zh: 你有什么方法让孩子们吃健康食品？

sentences.en: You educate them about the health benefits of the food.
sentences.zh: 你告诉他们这种食物对健康有什么好处。

sentences.en: But is this actually a good idea?
sentences.zh: 但这真的是个好主意吗？

sentences.en: New social science research suggests maybe not.
sentences.zh: 新的社会科学研究表明可能并非如此。

sentences.en: Uh-oh.
sentences.zh: 噢，糟糕。

sentences.en: Mihal May Maran at Northwestern and Islet Fishbach at the University of Chicago
sentences.zh: 西北大学的米哈尔·梅·马兰和芝加哥大学的伊斯莱特·费什巴赫

sentences.en: find that children who are told that crackers are healthy
sentences.zh: 发现，当孩子们被告知饼干很健康时，

sentences.en: infer that this means the crackers are not yummy and they eat less of them.
sentences.zh: 他们会推断这意味着饼干不好吃，于是吃得更少了。

sentences.en: The researchers tried another experiment with carrots.
sentences.zh: 研究人员又用胡萝卜做了另一个实验。

sentences.en: They told preschoolers that eating carrots would help them become better readers.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉学龄前儿童，吃胡萝卜能帮助他们成为更好的读者。

sentences.en: Again, they find that creating this kind of instrumental goal
sentences.zh: 结果他们再次发现，创造这种工具性的目标，

sentences.en: causes the preschoolers to eat fewer carrots.
sentences.zh: 会导致学龄前儿童吃更少的胡萝卜。

sentences.en: Basically, the researchers think that when preschoolers are given one kind of association,
sentences.zh: 基本上，研究人员认为，当学龄前儿童被给予某种关联时，

sentences.en: crackers are healthy or carrots help you with reading,
sentences.zh: 比如“饼干很健康”或“胡萝卜有助于阅读”，

sentences.en: they unconsciously infer that alternate associations must be weaker,
sentences.zh: 他们会下意识地推断其他的关联必然较弱，

sentences.en: that the carrots and the crackers can't be tasty.
sentences.zh: 即胡萝卜和饼干肯定不好吃。

sentences.en: The moral of the story is, if you want kids to eat certain kinds of food,
sentences.zh: 这个故事的寓意是，如果你想让孩子们吃某种食物，

sentences.en: sell the tastiness of the food rather than the health benefits.
sentences.zh: 要推销食物的美味，而不是它的健康益处。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So sell the steak, not the sizzle.
sentences.zh: 所以要卖牛排，而不是卖滋滋声。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I also think another factor that could be at work here is that any child who hears an adult say
sentences.zh: 我还认为这里起作用的另一个因素是，任何听到成年人说

sentences.en: that carrots will make you a better reader knows that is not an adult they could ever truSt.
sentences.zh: “吃胡萝卜会让你成为更好的读者”的孩子，都知道那个成年人是不可信的。

sentences.en: In other words, kids are just good lie detectors.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，孩子们是很好的测谎仪。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Kids are good lie detectors no matter what they eat.
sentences.zh: 无论吃什么，孩子们都是很好的测谎仪。

sentences.en: But it is interesting because we do.
sentences.zh: 但这很有趣，因为我们确实会这样做。

sentences.en: I mean, I remember when my kids were growing up, you do want them to eat healthy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得我孩子们长大时，你确实希望他们吃得健康。

sentences.en: And so you're not sure how to persuade them to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以你不确定该如何说服他们。

sentences.en: And so basically what you're saying is they push the good taste rather than the ancillary benefits.
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上是说，他们应该强调美味，而不是辅助性的好处。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think when we think about many things in human behavior, Dan,
sentences.zh: 丹，我认为当我们思考人类行为中的许多事情时，

sentences.en: I think we often assume that presenting the rational arguments to people is the best way to go.
sentences.zh: 我们往往认为向人们提出理性的论点是最好的方法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so if you're selling carrots, you sell the rational arguments that carrots are good for you.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在推销胡萝卜，你会推销理性的论点，即胡萝卜对你有好处。

sentences.en: The rational arguments don't always work and sometimes they backfire.
sentences.zh: 理性的论点并不总是有效，有时还会适得其反。

sentences.en: Yeah, especially when it comes to eating.
sentences.zh: 是的，尤其是在饮食方面。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's see if this rational argument has any benefits.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看这个理性的论点是否有任何好处。

sentences.en: Dan, if you're going to be done on time, you have to do your next segment on time
sentences.zh: 丹，如果你想按时完成，你就必须按时完成你的下一个环节，

sentences.en: and your next 60 seconds starts right now.
sentences.zh: 你接下来的60秒现在开始。

sentences.en: Well, as we've discussed, all kinds of hidden forces affect how much we eat.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我们所讨论的，各种隐藏的力量都会影响我们的进食量。

sentences.en: But here's one I didn't expect, the weight of your waiter or waitress.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一个我没想到的因素：你的服务员的体重。

sentences.en: Oh, boy.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Tim Durring of the University of Göttingen in Germany and Cornell's Brian Wansink,
sentences.zh: 德国哥廷根大学的蒂姆·杜林和康奈尔大学的布莱恩·万辛克，

sentences.en: one of the leading scholars of eating behavior, went to more than 50 restaurants in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 他是饮食行为领域的顶尖学者之一，走访了美国50多家餐厅，

sentences.en: from chains like Applebee's and Olive Garden to smaller independent establishments,
sentences.zh: 从像Applebee's和Olive Garden这样的连锁店到较小的独立餐厅，

sentences.en: and they looked at interactions between diners and servers.
sentences.zh: 他们观察了食客和服务员之间的互动。

sentences.en: They found that customers were four times as likely to order dessert
sentences.zh: 他们发现，当服务员的身体质量指数（BMI）较高时，

sentences.en: when they were served by waitstaff with high body mass indexes than those with low BMIs.
sentences.zh: 顾客点甜点的可能性是服务员BMI较低时的四倍。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: People also ordered more alcohol from heavy servers than from slimmer ones,
sentences.zh: 人们从体型较胖的服务员那里点的酒也比从较瘦的服务员那里点的多，

sentences.en: and the BMI of the diners themselves didn't matter at all.
sentences.zh: 而且食客自己的BMI完全没有影响。

sentences.en: Now, this is what's called an observational study.
sentences.zh: 现在，这被称为观察性研究。

sentences.en: It wasn't a controlled experiment.
sentences.zh: 它不是一项对照实验。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that heavy waiters necessarily cause people to order the apple chimmy cheesecake.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着胖服务员必然导致人们去点苹果芝士蛋糕。

sentences.en: Still, it shows once again how quiet factors, the setting we're in,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，它再次表明，安静的因素、我们所处的环境、

sentences.en: the social cues around us can influence what we do and even what we eat.
sentences.zh: 我们周围的社交暗示是如何影响我们的行为，甚至影响我们吃什么的。

sentences.en: Here's a question for you, Dan.
sentences.zh: 丹，我有个问题要问你。

sentences.en: If I want to avoid this kind of bias,
sentences.zh: 如果我想避免这种偏见，

sentences.en: do you think it makes sense for me to decide what I'm going to order
sentences.zh: 你认为在我点餐之前就决定好我要点什么，

sentences.en: before the waiter actually shows up at my table?
sentences.zh: 在服务员来到我的桌子前就决定好，这有意义吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对有意义。

sentences.en: There's a lot of evidence in eating and even in other kinds of behaviors
sentences.zh: 在饮食甚至其他行为方面有很多证据表明，

sentences.en: that when we make better decisions, when we make them in advance,
sentences.zh: 当我们做出更好的决定时，当我们提前做出决定时，

sentences.en: rather than at that moment of truth
sentences.zh: 而不是在那个关键时刻，

sentences.en: when the triple brownie explosion melt is staring us in the face.
sentences.zh: 当三重布朗尼爆炸熔岩蛋糕摆在我们面前时。

sentences.en: I like that because, of course, there's all this research showing that we make better decisions
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个说法，因为当然，有大量的研究表明，我们为未来的自己

sentences.en: for our future cells.
sentences.zh: 做出的决定会更好。

sentences.en: And so I'm going to tell you right now, Dan,
sentences.zh: 所以丹，我现在要告诉你，

sentences.en: I'm going to stick to my next 60-second deadline on my next Stop What Science segment.
sentences.zh: 在我的下一个“秒表科学”环节，我会坚持我的60秒期限。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to set the timer, and it's going off right now.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我要设置计时器了，现在就开始。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This is a study that makes me very happy.
sentences.zh: 这项研究让我非常高兴。

sentences.en: If you're on a diet, should you allow yourself to cheat?
sentences.zh: 如果你在节食，你应该允许自己作弊吗？

sentences.en: The rational answer is no.
sentences.zh: 理性的回答是：不。

sentences.en: The hidden brain answer is yes.
sentences.zh: “隐藏的大脑”给出的回答是：是的。

sentences.en: A study in the Journal of Consumer Psychology finds that when dieters are told
sentences.zh: 《消费者心理学杂志》上的一项研究发现，当节食者被告知

sentences.en: they can have a day off each week from their diets,
sentences.zh: 他们每周可以有一天从节食中休息，

sentences.en: when they can eat whatever they want, this is a day of planned cheating,
sentences.zh: 可以随心所欲地吃东西，这就是所谓的“计划性作弊日”，

sentences.en: they did just as well when it came to losing weight
sentences.zh: 他们在减重方面的表现，

sentences.en: as dieters who didn't give themselves any room to cheat.
sentences.zh: 和那些不给自己任何作弊空间的节食者一样好。

sentences.en: Even better, the dieters who cheated reported being happier with their diets
sentences.zh: 更好的是，那些作弊的节食者报告说对自己的饮食更满意，

sentences.en: and maybe would stick to them much longer.
sentences.zh: 而且可能坚持的时间会更长。

sentences.en: The researchers have a wonderful academic euphemism to describe this kind of cheating.
sentences.zh: 研究人员用了一个非常棒的学术委婉语来描述这种作弊。

sentences.en: They call these hedonic deviations.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“享乐偏差”。

sentences.en: The important thing to remember here is that the cheating has to be planned and deliberate.
sentences.zh: 这里要记住的重要一点是，作弊必须是计划好的、深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: Most diets end with a crash, and when you crash, you feel like you failed.
sentences.zh: 大多数节食以崩溃告终，当你崩溃时，你会觉得自己失败了。

sentences.en: When you plan your hedonic deviations, it's not a crash.
sentences.zh: 当你计划好你的“享乐偏差”时，那不是崩溃。

sentences.en: It's just a controlled landing before you take off again.
sentences.zh: 那只是在再次起飞前的一次受控着陆。

sentences.en: It puts you in charge, makes you happier, might have long-term health benefits.
sentences.zh: 它让你掌握主动权，让你更快乐，可能还有长期的健康益处。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's quite fascinating.
sentences.zh: 是的，这非常迷人。

sentences.en: I actually think that some of it also has to do with autonomy,
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为其中一些也与自主权有关，

sentences.en: that when you're on a diet, you're very controlled.
sentences.zh: 当你节食时，你受到严格的控制。

sentences.en: And so if you have this escape valve where you're in control just for one day,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个逃生阀，让你在一天之内掌握控制权，

sentences.en: that can probably make you feel better and probably boost adherence.
sentences.zh: 那可能会让你感觉更好，并可能提高坚持度。

sentences.en: I also love the idea of the hedonic deviation.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢“享乐偏差”这个概念。

sentences.en: I think that I like to consider stopwatch science a hedonic deviation
sentences.zh: 我想我愿意把“秒表科学”看作是美国听众生活中的一种“享乐偏差”。

sentences.en: in the lives of American listeners.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你，丹，我想下次我会更好地控制我的时间，

sentences.en: I tell you what, I think I'm going to stick to my time better the next time, Dan,
sentences.zh: 如果偶尔，也许每两周一次，你给我两分钟来做“秒表科学”的话。

sentences.en: if occasionally, maybe once every two weeks, you give me two minutes to do a stopwatch science.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们可以为“秒表科学”设立一个作弊日。

sentences.en: Okay, we can have a cheat day for stopwatch science.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以就是这样。

sentences.en: All right, so there you have it.
sentences.zh: 买一张大桌子，把你的食物切成小块。

sentences.en: Buy a big table and cut your food into tiny pieces.
sentences.zh: 注意你的同伴，或者用丹的话说，和男人一起吃饭，而不是女人。

sentences.en: Be mindful of your eating companions, or as Dan would put it, eat with men, not women.
sentences.zh: 早餐吃得丰盛，晚餐不要吃得太丰盛。

sentences.en: Eat a big breakfast, not a big dinner.
sentences.zh: 告诉孩子们蔬菜很美味，而不是很健康。

sentences.en: Tell kids vegetables are tasty and not very healthy.
sentences.zh: 去餐厅时要有一个经验法则。

sentences.en: Have a rule of thumb when you go to a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 一杯饮料，一份主菜。

sentences.en: One drink, one entree.
sentences.zh: 如果你要节食，计划偶尔放纵一下自己。

sentences.en: And if you're going on a diet, plan on indulging yourself once in a while.
sentences.zh: 这就是全部内容。

sentences.en: Dan Ping, thank you for joining me on Stopwatch Science.
sentences.zh: 丹·平，感谢你参加《秒表科学》节目。

sentences.en: Always a pleasure, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: The Hidden Brain Podcast is produced by Cara McGurk-Allison, Maggie Penman, and Max Nestrack.
sentences.zh: 《隐藏的大脑》播客由卡拉·麦格克-艾利森、玛吉·彭曼和马克斯·内斯特拉克制作。

sentences.en: Find more Hidden Brain on Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram,
sentences.zh: 欢迎在 Facebook、Twitter 和 Instagram 上关注《隐藏的大脑》，

sentences.en: and hear my stories on your local public radio station.
sentences.zh: 也可以在当地公共广播电台收听我的故事。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆，这里是 NPR。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: You should try out the new NPR One app for your phone for conversations you won't hear anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 你应该试试手机上的全新 NPR One 应用，那里有你在别处听不到的对话。

sentences.en: This week, Guy Raz interviews TED curator Chris Anderson,
sentences.zh: 本周，盖伊·拉兹采访了 TED 策展人克里斯·安德森，

sentences.en: where they discuss the secrets to giving a great TED talk.
sentences.zh: 他们探讨了发表精彩 TED 演讲的秘诀。

sentences.en: Search for TED Radio on the NPR One app,
sentences.zh: 在 NPR One 应用中搜索“TED Radio”，

sentences.en: where you can also find stories from your local station and more great podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你还可以在那里找到来自当地电台的故事以及更多精彩播客。

sentences.en: NPR One is in the App Store now.
sentences.zh: NPR One 现已上架 App Store。
